'''Obaid Siddiqi''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (7 January 1932&nbsp;– 26 July 2013) was an Indian National Research Professor and the Founder-Director of the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) [[National Center for Biological Sciences]]. He made seminal contributions to the field of behavioural neurogenetics using the [[Drosophila melanogaster#History of use in genetic analysis|genetics]] and [[neurobiology]] of [[Drosophila]].

==Early life and education==
Obaid Siddiqi was born in 1932 in [[Basti district]] of [[Uttar Pradesh]]. He received his early education at [[Aligarh Muslim University]] where he completed his MSc<ref>{{Cite web|title=SCIENTIST AND INTELLECTUAL – Obaid Siddiqi and his larger family|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/opinion/scientist-and-intellectual-obaid-siddiqi-and-his-larger-family/cid/273645|access-date=2021-04-05|website=The Telegraph|location=Kolkata}}</ref> He completed his PhD at the [[University of Glasgow]], under the supervision of [[Guido Pontecorvo]]. He carried out his post doctoral research at the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]], and [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.ncbs.res.in/archivednews/story/catalyst-culture-creativity|title=Catalyst of a Culture of Creativity &#124; NCBS news|website=news.ncbs.res.in}}</ref> He was invited by [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]] to set up the molecular biology unit at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) in [[Bombay]] in 1962. Thirty years later, he became the founding director of the TIFR [[National Center for Biological Sciences]] in [[Bangalore]], where he would continue his research into his final days of life.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iiap.res.in/obaidsiddiqi|title=Prof. Obaid Siddiqi|access-date=7 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011073051/https://www.iiap.res.in/obaidsiddiqi|archive-date=11 October 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Research==
Siddiqi's studies in the field of neurogenetics unravelled the link between genes, behaviour and the brain. In the 1970s, his work with Seymour Benzer<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tanouye |first1=Mark A. |title=Seymour Benzer 1921–2007 |journal=Nature Genetics |date=February 2008 |volume=40 |issue=2 |pages=121 |doi=10.1038/ng0208-121 |pmid=18227864 |pmc=2655269 }}</ref> at Caltech led to the discovery of temperature-sensitive paralytic Drosophila mutants and the generation and transmission of neural signals.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/obaid-siddiqi | title=Obaid Siddiqi &#124; the Best of Indian Science | access-date=2 June 2020 | archive-date=2 April 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230402075635/http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/obaid-siddiqi | url-status=dead }}</ref> This heralded the dawn of the field of neurogenetics.

At TIFR, Siddiqi and his graduate student, Veronica Rodrigues,<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://news.ncbs.res.in/archivednews/story/veronica-rodrigues-1953-2010 |title = Veronica Rodrigues 1953-2010 &#124; NCBS news}}</ref> isolated and characterized the first collection of mutants with defects in smell and taste in Drosophila. Siddiqi's work in neurogenetics led to the foundational advances in understanding how taste and smell are detected and encoded in the brain.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Obaid Siddiqi - Who transformed molecular biology research in India? | url=https://vigyanprasar.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/DreamOctober2013Eng.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126014358/http://vigyanprasar.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/DreamOctober2013Eng.pdf | archive-date=26 November 2018 | access-date=2 June 2020 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Death==
Siddiqi died on 26 July 2013 in Bangalore following a freak road accident on 21 July 2013 which caused severe damage to the brain. He is survived by his wife Asiya, sons [[Imran Siddiqi|Imran]] and Kaleem, and daughters Yumna and Diba.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/acclaimed-scientist-obaid-siddiqi-no-more/article4957261.ece|title=Acclaimed scientist Obaid Siddiqi no more|work=[[The Hindu]]|place=Bangalore|date=27 July 2013|access-date=14 December 2017}}</ref>
